BBQR AUTOMATED HPLC ANALYSER FOR HbA1c & HbA2 1. Benchtop, Automated, integrated dedicated HPLC system to measure H bA1c, HbA2 and other Hb variant. 2. System should be based on Cation-Exchange HPLC. 3. The system should have a dual program/single run mode to perform eith er HbA1c or HbA2/ HbF/ other variants. 4. The system should be able to screen and quantitative variant hemoglobi n’s eg HbA2, HbA, HbF and detect most commonly occurring abnormal he moglobins like HbS, HbD, HbE, HbC, HbQ. 5. The system should have traceable reference standards for instruments c alibration ensuring accurate quantization of results. For HbA1c results shou ld be traceable to reference methods through NGSP/ IFCC certification and be able to detect A1c values in presence of abnormal hemoglobin variants. 6. System should be equipped with automated sample loading with minim al manual intervention. 7. The equipment should have the provision for automatic mixing of blood sample prior to actual testing by inversion of test tubes/other means. 8. System should be able to use whole blood sample using not more than 5 0µL of whole blood sample and 150 µL of diluted sample. 9. It should have an offline/online library which should be a searchable dat abase with chromatograms of fully classified abnormal hemoglobin and tha lassemia. 10 System should be equipped for loading minimum of 10 samples at a tim e. 11. System should have throughout of 10 or more samples/hour for HbA1c and 6 or more samples/hour for hemoglobinopathy. 12. Should have automatic generation of chromatogram with peak identific ation and percentage quantification. 13. System should be able to detect HbA1c between 3-20 %. The reportabl e range for HbA2 should be 2.0%-10.0%. The reportable range for HbF sho uld be 1.0% - 40% 14 It should be able to print a hard copy report giving identification and inf ormation on the subtype and quantity of hemoglobin detected. 15. Reagents should be provided with buffers in transparent plastic tanks or visible on screen the status of them to view the level of buffers columns, primers, calibrators & sample vials. 16 The system should have a visible alarm system for low buffer in the mo bile phase reservoirs, low level value for cartridge injections as well as buil t in alarms for calibration failure. 17. System should freely run manually diluted samples without any need o f sample cup adapters. 18. System should maintain the column/ capillary at an ambient temperatu re and does not need temperature optimization for every change of kit.

19. The system should have a bi-directional LIS. The system should be CE/ FDA/ BIS Indian standards approved. 20. System should be able to store more than 500 patient results with auto matic data backup and recovery. 21. The company should be able to provide normal and abnormal controls for HbA2, HbF and HbA1c and provide quality control program to help com pare results with similar user worldwide. 22. The system should be supplied with 02 KVA UPS with at least half hour power back up. 23. The system should be inclusive of 05 Years warranty from the date of i nstallation and 05 years CAMC post warranty. 24. The system should be provided with 1000 HbA1C and 500Hb screening along with controls (HbA1c and Hb variants controls). The system should b e supplied with standards/ calibrators for instrument ensuring accurate qua ntization of results. 25. The company should have dedicated team to provide technical training at time of installation and well trained engineers to provide service, includi ng preventive maintenance and easy access for replacement of consumabl es and maintenance throughout. BBQR AUTOMATED HPLC ANALYSER FOR HbA1c & HbA2 1. Benchtop, Automated, integrated dedicated HPLC system to measure H bA1c, HbA2 and other Hb variant. 2. System should be based on Cation-Exchange HPLC. 3. The system should have a dual program/single run mode to perform eith er HbA1c or HbA2/ HbF/ other variants. 4. The system should be able to screen and quantitative variant hemoglobi n’s eg HbA2, HbA, HbF and detect most commonly occurring abnormal he moglobins like HbS, HbD, HbE, HbC, HbQ. 5. The system should have traceable reference standards for instruments c alibration ensuring accurate quantization of results. For HbA1c results shou ld be traceable to reference methods through NGSP/ IFCC certification and be able to detect A1c values in presence of abnormal hemoglobin variants. 6. System should be equipped with automated sample loading with minim al manual intervention. 7. The equipment should have the provision for automatic mixing of blood sample prior to actual testing by inversion of test tubes/other means. 8. System should be able to use whole blood sample using not more than 5 0µL of whole blood sample and 150 µL of diluted sample. 9. It should have an offline/online library which should be a searchable dat abase with chromatograms of fully classified abnormal hemoglobin and tha lassemia. 10 System should be equipped for loading minimum of 10 samples at a tim e. 11. System should have throughout of 10 or more samples/hour for HbA1c and 6 or more samples/hour for hemoglobinopathy. 12. Should have automatic generation of chromatogram with peak identific ation and percentage quantification. 13. System should be able to detect HbA1c between 3-20 %. The reportabl e range for HbA2 should be 2.0%-10.0%. The reportable range for HbF sho uld be 1.0% - 40% 14 It should be able to print a hard copy report giving identification and inf ormation on the subtype and quantity of hemoglobin detected. 15. Reagents should be provided with buffers in transparent plastic tanks or visible on screen the status of them to view the level of buffers columns, primers, calibrators & sample vials. 16 The system should have a visible alarm system for low buffer in the mo bile phase reservoirs, low level value for cartridge injections as well as buil t in alarms for calibration failure. 17. System should freely run manually diluted samples without any need o f sample cup adapters. 18. System should maintain the column/ capillary at an ambient temperatu re and does not need temperature optimization for every change of kit.

19. The system should have a bi-directional LIS. The system should be CE/ FDA/ BIS Indian standards approved. 20. System should be able to store more than 500 patient results with auto matic data backup and recovery. 21. The company should be able to provide normal and abnormal controls for HbA2, HbF and HbA1c and provide quality control program to help com pare results with similar user worldwide. 22. The system should be supplied with 02 KVA UPS with at least half hour power back up. 23. The system should be inclusive of 05 Years warranty from the date of i nstallation and 05 years CAMC post warranty. 24. The system should be provided with 1000 HbA1C and 500Hb screening along with controls (HbA1c and Hb variants controls). The system should b e supplied with standards/ calibrators for instrument ensuring accurate qua ntization of results. 25. The company should have dedicated team to provide technical training at time of installation and well trained engineers to provide service, includi ng preventive maintenance and easy access for replacement of consumabl es and maintenance throughout.
